date: Nov 19, 2026 · Week 2 / Day 4 · Decision-driven meetings and tradeoffs

cards.title: Define the stop line first
cards.question: PCIe margin is positive in simulation but close to the limit. What evidence makes this a go, conditional go, or hold?
cards.selfCheck: Set the required margin and correlation confidence before reviewing plots. Exercise: state a conditional release gate in 25 seconds, including who can approve the exception.
cards.prompt: Role-play a PCIe release-gate meeting. Challenge me to set measurable go/hold thresholds, decision authority and an escalation trigger.

cards.title: Trade in system outcomes
cards.question: Layout offers a longer return path to avoid a connector re-spin. How do you compare schedule benefit with SI risk?
cards.selfCheck: Translate the routing change into channel impact and validation effort, not just trace length. Exercise: present two options and recommend one with a deadline.
cards.prompt: Act as a skeptical layout lead and program manager. Coach me to negotiate a connector-routing tradeoff using system consequences and a bounded decision.

cards.title: Time-box the unresolved
cards.question: Lab wants another TDR sweep; modeling says the discrepancy is harmless. What do you decide before the meeting ends?
cards.selfCheck: Name the decision that depends on the mismatch, the minimum discriminating measurement and a time-boxed owner. Exercise: close the discussion in 30 seconds without pretending consensus.
cards.prompt: Simulate a tense EM-versus-TDR review. Test whether I can acknowledge dissent, select decisive evidence and record a closure criterion.

cards.title: An owner is not a handoff
cards.question: A PDN peak spans VRM, package and PCB. Each team offers analysis, but no one owns the release recommendation. What is your move?
cards.selfCheck: Assign one integrator accountable for the system droop verdict while preserving domain owners for evidence. Exercise: write a one-sentence decision record with dependencies and checkpoint.
cards.prompt: Coach me through assigning cross-functional PDN ownership without formal authority. Press for a named integrator, deliverables and a decision date.

cards.title: Interrupt the status parade
cards.question: In a crosstalk review, five engineers report progress but nobody asks for a decision. How do you reset the room?
cards.selfCheck: Revisit Week 1 risk-first framing: summarize exposure, then ask for the decision, options and accountable approver. Exercise: deliver a 20-second interruption and a 20-second closeout.
cards.prompt: Role-play a meandering crosstalk meeting. Interrupt me as stakeholders do, then grade my risk-first reset, tradeoff recommendation and decision closeout.
